Analysis: Hypothesis 1 draws on a well‐established link between chronic inflammation and altered biomolecular processes in the liver—connecting cytokine signaling to changes in glycosylation and oncogenic progression. Although it lacks specificity in identifying the exact cytokines and glycosyltransferases involved, its overall framework is more directly tied to known pathological mechanisms in HCC. This makes it relatively more plausible and testable despite its moderate novelty. While Hypothesis 2 offers a more innovative multi‐omics approach by integrating gut microbiome dysbiosis with hepatocyte epigenetics to modulate AFP-L3 production, its proposed mechanistic pathways are less clearly defined, making the experimental design more complex and its direct causality and safety profile harder to assess. In summary, based on the criteria of novelty, plausibility, testability, and safety, Hypothesis 1 is superior.
